components.description: Amphenol NDAAFR QSFP28 to QSFP28 100G passive direct-attach copper cable, one end - 32 AWG eight-pair PVC-jacketed cable and a green lanyard pull. It composes generic/qsfp-cable@1 and sets the lanyard's colour; the shape is the generic's.
components.name: qsfp28-passive-dac

components.description: Amphenol NJAAF3 QSFP56 to QSFP56 200G active copper cable, one end - 30 AWG eight-pair dual-drain cable in a black PVC jacket, with a blue lanyard pull. It composes generic/qsfp-cable@1 and sets the lanyard and jacket colours; the shape is the generic's.
components.name: qsfp56-linear-active

components.description: Rear face of the alarm card of a passive Amphenol Network Solutions 300CB08 - two three-pin wire-wrap headers, one per side, carrying the Form C alarm relay contacts. Replacement part 307608.
components.name: alarm-card-307608

components.description: Eight-position DIP switch seen through a slot in the front of an Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU power panel - one slide switch per breaker position on that side, down to enable its alarm and up to silence an empty position. Drawn with all eight UP, which is OFF and is how a panel with no breakers fitted has to be set.
components.name: alarm-dip-8

components.description: Single-pole bullet-terminal plug-in circuit breaker for Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU breaker panels - the bare breaker, with its handle, the rating printed on the handle and an I/O legend beside it. It ships into the panel wearing a touch guard, which is a separate part seated on it. The panel datasheet calls the breaker AIRPAX 1U Series and sells eleven ratings from 2 A to 60 A, standard delay.

rating.description: trip rating in amperes; each value is a separate vendor part number, listed under provenance
rating.label: Rating

state.description: where the handle is; a trip puts it at OFF, so tripped is drawn as off
state.label: State

components.name: breaker-1ru
components.size-notes: THE FACE IS THE OPENING IT SHOWS THROUGH, not the whole breaker. the 300CB08 installation guide 149722-2 A9 Fig. 3-1 draws sixteen openings 17.8 wide by 39.1 high on a 19.81 pitch. The breaker behind is 19.05 MAX wide by 37.03 MAX high in the Sensata IAR/IUR/IER/CUR/CER datasheet, pages 2 and 3, so its sides sit behind the webs of the front cover and it is drawn 37.0 high, centred in the opening. The depth is dimension B for a quarter-inch bullet, 5.019 in or 127.48, front of the body to the bullet tips, handle excluded - an estimate, because the five-sixteenth bullet is 129.35 and no document held says which the panel takes.

components.description: Blanking cover for an unused breaker position on an Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU breaker panel. A sheet of sixteen ships with the panel and more are part number 149568.
components.name: breaker-blank-1ru
components.size-notes: The cover closes one opening of the front cover, so it takes the cell that the 300CB08 installation guide 149722-2 A9 Fig. 3-1 draws: 17.8 by 39.1. The thickness is a guess at a moulded plate; Fig. 2-12 shows it as a thin part and gives no dimension.

components.description: Captive thumbscrew holding the removable front cover of an Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU power panel - turned by hand or with a Phillips driver.
components.name: cover-thumbscrew

components.description: The two threaded inserts in the face of a 1RU plug-in breaker, one above the other - where its touch guard screws on, and where the breaker puller threads in once the guard is off.
components.name: guard-mount-1ru
components.size-notes: The inserts are 29.11 apart, centre to centre, in the Sensata IAR/IUR/IER/CUR/CER datasheet, pages 2 and 3; 32.3 is that plus one insert. Their 3.2 diameter is read by eye off the product photograph of a bare breaker; the datasheet gives the thread, 6-32, and not the insert.

components.description: One DC feed input of an Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU power panel with horizontal inputs - two busbar landings side by side, one BATTERY and one RETURN, that run straight back from the panel so the input cables leave to the rear. Each landing takes a dual-hole lug on 3/8 inch holes.
components.name: input-feed-busbar
components.size-notes: the 300CB08 installation guide 149722-2 A9 Fig. 3-8 at 2.849 px/mm: the input assembly is framed 42.5 wide by 30.6 high (121 px by 87 px), with the two landings seen end-on as slots 6.0 and 7.7 wide and 24.9 high, and two bolt heads between them.

components.description: One DC feed input of an Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU power panel with vertical inputs - its BATT terminal and its RTN terminal side by side, each two 3/8-16 studs taking a dual-hole lug. One feed, both poles: side A is one of these and side B is another.
components.name: input-feed-studs
components.size-notes: Two stud terminals 35.1 apart, centre to centre, in the 300CB08 installation guide 149722-2 A9 Fig. 3-6: their centres read 14.7 and 49.8 from the edge of the rear face (3.2006 px/mm). Each terminal is amphenol-ns/input-stud-pair@1, 29.0 wide, so the pair spans 64.1.

components.description: One input terminal of an Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU power panel with vertical inputs - two 3/8-16 studs one above the other on 1 inch centres, taking a dual-hole compression lug up to 1.15 inch wide.
components.name: input-stud-pair

components.description: Rear centre block of an Amphenol Network Solutions nrgILS power panel: a dark plate lettered nrgNET, with the two nrgNET RJ45s stacked IN over OUT on the left, and on the right a probe jack over three small white headers. It takes the place the passive panel gives its alarm card.
components.name: nrg-ils-rear-block
components.size-notes: The opening the 300CB08 installation guide 149722-2 A9 gives the centre block of every 300CB08 rear (Fig. 3-6, 39.0 by 42.8). The only image of this block is the rear photograph in the nrgILS300CB08 datasheet (Fig. 2), a 790 px three-quarter view in which the plate spans about 65 px, so nothing inside it is measured: every position below is a fraction of the plate read by eye, good to two millimetres at best.

components.description: Front display of an nrgSMART integrated controller - a two-line black and white OLED that scrolls the controller name, nrgOS version, active panel count, IP address, panel name and serial, feed currents and voltages and the two probe temperatures, and flashes between white and black backgrounds on an alarm.
components.name: nrg-oled

components.description: Rear centre block of an Amphenol Network Solutions nrgSMART power panel with an integrated controller or sensor card: the two alarm relay headers of the plain panel, and below them two nrgNET connectors, IN over OUT, and two nrgTEMP probe jacks.
components.name: nrg-rear-block
components.size-notes: The centre block of the 300CB08 installation guide 149722-2 A9 Fig. 3-7, the same 39.0 by 42.8 the plain panel gives its alarm card in Fig. 3-6. The connectors inside it are placed from a threefold enlargement of that figure, about 3.2 px/mm before enlarging, so each is good to a millimetre and no better.

components.description: One connectorized output circuit of an Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU power panel - a two-pole latching receptacle, BATT above RTN, that takes a P40 plug (Amphenol PRM series, 4 mm contacts). Plugs are sold separately as kits 150325, 150326 and 152799.
components.name: output-p40
components.size-notes: the 300CB08 installation guide 149722-2 A9 Fig. 3-10: sixteen receptacles on a 13.41 pitch (38.33 px at 2.858 px/mm), each 10.5 wide by 29.8 high. The plug that mates it is 9.7 wide by 34.2 high in the customer drawing of the PRM0400 plug, which fits the width; the plug stands taller than the receptacle's drawn frame because its latch arms pass outside it.

components.description: One output circuit of an Amphenol Network Solutions 1RU power panel with terminal-block outputs - a BATT screw above an RTN screw, each a #10-32 taking a single-hole lug up to half an inch wide.
components.name: output-terminal

components.description: The P40 output plug of an Amphenol Network Solutions power panel - the Amphenol PRM series two-pole latching plug, PRM0400, 4 mm RADSOK contacts - wired, seen from the wire side as a front elevation sees it seated: the black housing, the two latch arms above and below it, and a short straight stub of insulated wire leaving each pole, BATT over RTN. Seats in a `p40` receptacle at its own mate point. It carries one wire per pole, not one cable.
components.name: p40-plug
components.size-notes: the end view of the Amphenol customer drawing PRM SERIES FEMALE, PLUG SIDE 4MM, rev A1 (4 JAN 20), dimensions it 0.38 in [9.7] wide and 1.35 in [34.2] high, the height across the two latch arms.

components.description: Touch guard cover for a 1RU plug-in breaker on an Amphenol Network Solutions breaker panel - a black hood screwed over the breaker handle so a circuit is not switched by accident. One ships on every breaker; a replacement set of sixteen is part 307794.
components.name: touch-guard-1ru
components.size-notes: The guard as the panel front view draws it: the 300CB08 installation guide 149722-2 A9 Fig. 3-1 shows sixteen guard cells 17.8 wide by 39.1 high (35 px and 77 px at 1.9685 px/mm), one filling each opening of the front cover.

components.description: 1RU TPA fuse holder, part 307492 - a plug-in carrier that takes one Cooper Bussmann TPA fuse and seats in the same position as a 1RU breaker on an Amphenol Network Solutions breaker or fuse panel. The fuse goes in through the side of the holder, behind a sliding cover, so nothing of it shows from the front: what the panel shows is the ribbed pull grip of the holder.

fuse-rating.description: rating of the TPA fuse fitted in the holder, in amperes; 0 for none. Each value is a separate vendor part number, listed under provenance
fuse-rating.label: Fuse

components.name: tpa-fuse-holder-307492
components.size-notes: BORROWED FROM amphenol-ns/breaker-1ru@1, because the holder fits the position a breaker fits (300CB08 datasheet: for use with TPA fuses, requires TPA fuse holder 307492) and no document held dimensions the holder itself. The face is the opening it shows through; the depth is the breaker's, front to bullet tips.

attrs.upstream: up to 85 MHz, 1 OFDMA and 6 ATDMA channels

components.description: Casa Bi-Directional Module, the original 85 MHz card. Carries no RF connectors at all; every port lands on the paired rear 6+12 I/O card. The faceplate is a blank plate with a model band, two tapering stripe groups and three status LEDs, shared with the BDM2 and BDM2m.
components.name: bdm
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

attrs.upstream: up to 204 MHz, 1 OFDMA and 6 ATDMA channels

components.description: Casa Bi-Directional Module 2 (BDM_204MHZ), the high-split 204 MHz card. Carries no RF connectors at all; every port lands on the paired rear 6+12 IO2 card. Faceplate shared with the BDM and BDM2m.
components.name: bdm2
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

attrs.upstream: up to 204 MHz, 1 OFDMA and 6 ATDMA channels

components.description: Casa Bi-Directional Module 2m (BDM2m_204MHZ), the high-split 204 MHz card with the newer packet processor. Carries no RF connectors at all; every port lands on the paired rear 6+12 IO2 card. Faceplate shared with the BDM and BDM2.
components.name: bdm2m
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa blank face plate for an unpopulated C100G or C40G card slot. A plain plate with two captive thumbscrews and nothing else. It is a functional part, not trim - it keeps the cooling airflow channelled through the chassis, and the guide is explicit that running a slot open makes components "excessively warm or even overheat". An empty bay in a real chassis has one of these in it.
components.name: blank-faceplate

components.description: The curved moulding on the C100G front bezel, between the casa systems mark and the model name. A closed lens-shaped outline, not a filled graphic.
components.name: brand-swoop

components.description: Casa C40G AC input panel - the bolted panel across the bottom of the REAR face on an AC chassis, where a DC chassis carries its two power entry modules. One continuous panel, not four module ends: it carries a rocker ON/OFF switch and an IEC C14 inlet for each of the four front-loaded PSUs, with vent mesh above and below.
components.name: c40g-ac-inlet-panel

components.description: Casa C40G system fan module, RIGHT-hand position. A tall side-mounted assembly of eight fan units with the air filter built into its outboard face, occupying the full height of the card band, and the air INTAKE for the chassis. The chassis takes two and they are NOT the same part: the left-hand position takes casa/c40g-fan-left@1, mechanically identical but printing the six card-slot numbers on its faceplate. That asymmetry is visible in every photograph and is why one part cannot serve both sides.
components.name: c40g-fan

components.description: Casa C40G LEFT fan module - the secondary position, and the one that carries the slot numbering. Mechanically the same tall side-mounted assembly as the right-hand system fan module, at the same 34.7 x 205, but its faceplate prints the six card-slot numbers 5 down to 0 with 3 and 2 in red, which the right-hand module does not.
components.name: c40g-fan-left

components.description: Casa C40G shelf ground terminal - the grounding landing in the left strip of the rear face, near the bottom. Three studs on a square grid, each a star washer under a hex nut, with the protective-earth mark printed in the fourth corner of that grid.
components.name: c40g-ground-studs

components.description: Casa C40G DC power entry module. Two sit side by side across the bottom of the rear face, each taking -40.5 to -60 VDC from a separate 20 A source and providing EMI filtering and redundant DC power to the chassis. The face carries a bolted terminal cover, four studs in a minus pair and a plus pair, two release levers and a disconnect-power warning.
components.name: c40g-pem

attrs.redundancy: up to four, concurrent; the C40G-20 needs at least two

components.description: Casa C40G AC power supply unit, 1100 W. Four sit in a row across the bottom front of the chassis behind the snap-on cover, numbered PSU1 to PSU4 from right to left. The front face carries two fans, a folding pull handle and a status LED; the ON/OFF switch and the AC inlet are on the module's other end, at the rear of the chassis.
components.name: c40g-psu-ac

components.description: Casa C40G snap-on power supply unit cover with integrated air filter - the full-width panel across the bottom of the front face, below the card band and the brand band. It covers the four AC PSU positions and carries the filter that protects them, and it snaps on rather than sliding into an opening.
components.name: c40g-psu-cover

components.description: Casa C100G front cable manager. Two brackets across the bottom of the front face, left and right, that carry the coax down and away from the exhaust.
components.name: cable-manager

components.description: Casa C100G/C40G chassis identity and compliance label, affixed to the top front of the chassis. Placeholder art - the blocks stand for the printed fields and no real model or serial is reproduced.
components.name: chassis-label

components.description: Casa CCAP Services Card (CSC8x10G) for the C100G/C40G CCAP chassis. Eight 10GbE SFP+ ports (XG0-XG7) in two ganged blocks of four, carrying the DOCSIS and EQAM MAC functions to Distributed Access nodes, plus a bank of eight two-lamp port rows and the STATUS, ACTIVE and ALARM cluster. Out-of-band signalling is on the separate optional CSC I/O card, not on this faceplate.
components.name: csc-8x10g
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa DS 8X192 downstream line card for the C100G/C40G CCAP chassis. DOCSIS QAM downstream module (DQM). Eight downstream QAM ports, but the RF connectors are on the paired rear RF Downstream I/O (RFD) module - this faceplate carries no connectors at all, only the STATUS, ALARM and ACTIVE lamps.
components.name: ds-8x192
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa DS 8X8 downstream line card for the C100G/C40G CCAP chassis. DOCSIS QAM downstream module (DQM). Eight downstream QAM ports, but the RF connectors are on the paired rear RF Downstream I/O (RFD) module - this faceplate carries no connectors at all, only the STATUS, ALARM and ACTIVE lamps.
components.name: ds-8x8
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa DS 8X96 downstream line card for the C100G/C40G CCAP chassis. DOCSIS QAM downstream module (DQM). Eight downstream QAM ports, but the RF connectors are on the paired rear RF Downstream I/O (RFD) module - this faceplate carries no connectors at all, only the STATUS, ALARM and ACTIVE lamps.
components.name: ds-8x96
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa C100G fan assembly module. Three sit side by side above the rear card band - LEFT, CENTER and RIGHT - and each contains two fans, designated 0 = front and 1 = back. The face is a punched perforation grid with a pull handle across the lower third and an indicator panel carrying a hot-swap button and HS / alarm / OK indicators. Maximum 100 W each, 300 W across the three.
components.name: fan

components.description: Casa C100G rear grounding lug landing. Two studs on 15.3 mm centres, each with a star washer under a hex nut, for a two-hole grounding lug.
components.name: ground-bolts

components.description: Casa C100G ESD strap receptacle. A marked plate carrying a 4 mm jack - the library's common/esd-jack@1, composed - and a chassis-ground symbol: you plug the wrist strap in rather than bolting to it. Appears on both faces, on the same physical side of the chassis - which reads as the RIGHT of the front view and the LEFT of the rear view.
components.name: ground-strap

components.description: Casa 6+12 I/O module - the rear half of a BDM position, carrying six downstream (D0-D5) and twelve upstream (U0-U11) MCX jacks. Pairs with a BDM in the associated front slot. The IO2 variant is the same faceplate at 5-204 MHz instead of 5-85 MHz. (v2 = composed - the eighteen MCX openings are std/mcx@1 at the sourced 4.95 x 4.50 D-hole; v1 drew them inline at an ESTIMATED 3.87 x 3.14, so an aperture here is about 28 percent wider than it was at v1. Jack AXES are unchanged.)
components.name: io-6p12
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa 6+12 IO2 module - the 204 MHz-capable rear half of a BDM2 or BDM2m position, carrying six downstream (D0-D5) and twelve upstream (U0-U11) MCX jacks. Same faceplate as the plain 6+12 IO; the difference is upstream spectrum, 5-204 MHz instead of 5-85 MHz, and therefore which BDM it pairs with.
components.name: io-6p12-io2
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa 6+12 SW I/O - the combined switch and I/O card. Same six downstream and twelve upstream MCX jacks as the plain 6+12, but it also carries the LC switch function, so it goes in the redundancy slot that a BDM scheme frees up: C100G rear 8, C40G rear 4. Its RF port section stands proud of the faceplate. (v2 = composed - the eighteen MCX openings are std/mcx@1 at the sourced 4.95 x 4.50 D-hole; v1 drew them inline at an ESTIMATED 3.88 x 3.88, so an aperture here is about 28 percent wider in x and 16 percent in y than it was at v1. Jack AXES are unchanged.)
components.name: io-6p12-sw
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa 6+12 SW-IO2 - the 204 MHz-capable combined switch and I/O card. Same eighteen MCX jacks and the same LC switch function as the plain 6+12 SW- IO, at 5-204 MHz, so it is what a 204 MHz BDM build puts in the redundancy slot a BDM scheme frees up: C100G rear 8, C40G rear 4.
components.name: io-6p12-sw-io2
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa LC Switch BDM (LC-SW-BDM) - the line-card switch for BDM redundancy. Goes in the rear slot that PROTECTS, which under the C100G 11+1 scheme is rear 5 and under the C40G 3+1 scheme is rear 1. A blank faceplate; it switches the RF path rather than presenting ports.
components.name: lc-sw-bdm
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa CSC Out-of-Band (OOB) 2+8 I/O module - the rear half of a CSC 8x10G position, carrying two Narrowband Digital Forward downstream jacks (NDF0, NDF1) and eight Narrowband Digital Return upstream jacks (NDR0-NDR7). It gives a Remote PHY deployment the SCTE 55-1 / 55-2 signalling path that two-way legacy set-top boxes still need: analogue OOB carriers are digitised in the headend and turned back into RF at the node. One NDF and one NDR as a set (NDF0 with NDR0) is the minimum connection; NDF1/NDR1 drive a second signalling device.
components.name: oob-2p8
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is inherited from the rear-card family and is IMPOSSIBLE for the same reason - see casa/io-6p12 provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa C-series Power Entry Module. Two per chassis, PEM B on the left and PEM A on the right when facing the rear. Each carries four 30 A power branches. A branch is a -48/-60 VDC feed with its return, landed on a pair of studs in one of the two terminal blocks, and protected by its own rocker circuit breaker in the row above. The faceplate draws a leader line from each branch's terminal-cover screw up to the breaker that protects it.
components.name: pem

components.description: Casa RF Downstream I/O module (RFD) - the rear half of a DQM position, carrying the eight downstream F-type ports for one DS 8x8, DS 8x96 or DS 8x192 line card in the paired front slot. Silkscreened QAM IO. It carries no electronics of its own that the guide describes; it is the mechanical and electrical QAM connection to the HFC network.
components.name: rfd
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa RF Upstream I/O module (RFU), 16x8 variant - the rear half of a DCU position, carrying sixteen upstream F-type ports at eight channels each for a US 16x8 or US 16x4 line card in the paired front slot. Silkscreened US IO. The UPS 32x4 I/O module is the other RFU and is a different card, not a skin of this one: it swaps all sixteen F ports for thirty-two MCX.
components.name: rfu-16x8
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: One stud of a Casa shelf ground terminal, seen end on: a star washer, the hex nut on it and the end of the threaded stud. It is the stud a ground lug is landed on, so it is where a lug seats: it presents the nominal `terminal-stud` interface on the stud axis, at the end of the stud. casa/c40g-ground-studs@1 composes one per stud.
components.name: shelf-ground-stud
components.size-notes: the star washer as casa/c40g-ground-studs@1 drew it before the stud became a part of its own, 10.8 across its points; that terminal lifted the washer, the nut and the stud from casa/ground-bolts@1

components.description: Casa standard SMM 2x10GE - the C100G/C40G Switch and Management Module in its original density. Eight GigE SFP (G0-G7) and two 10GigE SFP+ (XG2, XG1), a 10/100BASE-T management RJ45 at the top and an RS-232 console RJ45 at the bottom, plus STATUS, ACTIVE and ALARM lamps. components.name: smm-2x10g

components.description: Casa/CommScope SMM300G Switch and Management Module - the 300G supervisor for the C100G and C40G CCAP chassis. components.description: Casa high-density SMM 8x10GigE - the C100G/C40G supervisor and switch module. Eight 10GigE SFP+ (XG0-XG7), two GigE SFP (G0, G1), a 10/100BASE-T management RJ45 and an RS-232 console RJ45, plus STATUS, ACTIVE and ALARM LEDs.
components.name: smm-8x10g
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa SMM Switch BDM A. Carries a Power Supply Monitor window and prints its own slot on the faceplate. NOT interchangeable with the B card - A is C100G rear slot 6 and C40G rear slot 2.
components.name: smm-sw-bdm-a
components.size-notes: d 380.0 is IMPOSSIBLE - a front and a rear card mate at a midplane inside a 386.0 chassis and two at 380.0 need 760. See provenance/depth-known-wrong

components.description: Casa SMM Switch BDM B. As the A card but for the other SMM position - C100G rear slot 7, C40G rear slot 3. Not interchangeable with A.
components.name: smm-sw-bdm-b

components.description: Panel-mount LC duplex adapter - a bezel carrying two LC bores side by side, as used for Tx/Rx pairs on optical line cards. Distinct from sfp-lc-duplex, which is a pluggable transceiver.
components.name: lc-duplex-adapter

components.description: The ONE white cap FS ships over both ports of an FHD LC duplex adapter - 5.85 x 12.25 as read off that adapter, drawn here 12.25 x 5.85 on the canonical across axis, with a rounded-square inset moulded in front of each port. A duplex connector, not two simplex ones: it mates `lc-duplex` and seats on the adapter's own slot, at the midpoint of its two bores, so seating it and seating a simplex cap in a bore are mutually exclusive (L115). It was drawn as part of common/lc-duplex-v-adapter until @3 took it off; its figures move here unchanged. `common/` for the reason common/lc-boot@1 gives: no standard governs a cap's shape, only the interface it plugs.

The same body as common/lc-duplex-adapter@6 in outline, latch keyways up; what differs is the shutter in each bore.
components.name: lc-duplex-shuttered-adapter
components.size-notes: WIDTH IS MEASURED, on FS's render of SKU 105333 (105333.main.jpg), in panel_measure's frame as #503 and #506 corrected it: the adapters abut in pairs, three pairs to a row, and the pairs measure 26.42, 26.09 and 26.26 - a mean of 26.26, so 13.1 an adapter (13.13). The row is centred on the plate to 0.01 mm, the check that does not come from the tool. 105335.main.jpg reads within 0.25 and is not used. HEIGHT IS ESTIMATED, and it is not common/lc-duplex-adapter@6's 11.0. The rows abut and repeat every 11.31 in the width-scaled frame, but the render looks down on the cassette - the lid shows, putting the camera about 12-13 degrees up - which foreshortens heights by 2-3%. Corrected, the pitch is 11.6, and three rows fill 34.8 of the plate's 35.05, which is what the render shows, the blue running from the plate's top edge to its bottom. The plate's own height cannot settle it on this render: #506's tool reads it 4.01% tall and refuses it, the older tool read it 2.76% short. Until review this part said 11.0, reached by applying a frame correction the wrong way round and then taking the agreement with the other adapter as a check.

components.description: LC duplex panel adapter with its two ports STACKED VERTICALLY - the shell FS fits to FHD cassettes and adapter panels. components.size-notes: WIDTH AND HEIGHT ARE BOTH MEASURED, each with a spread of 0.00 across all six adapters on FS's face-on render of SKU 57016 - scaled on the 108.97 mm FHD faceplate and validated against its 35.05 mm height to 1.02%. components.description: Panel-mount MDC adapter, one small-form-factor body carrying FOUR fibre positions across its two ports (a "2-Port Duplex" adapter: each port is itself a duplex MDC connector), as fitted to an FS FHD MDC panel. components.description: Panel-mount MPO/MTP adapter - one opening in a bezel, as fitted to an FS FHD adapter panel. Twelve fibres by default; an MPO-8, -16 or -24 is the same adapter with a different ferrule, and says so by overriding `optical.positions` on its placement.

components.description: The grey dust cap FS ships in an MTP/MPO port - a 12.8 x 8.1 moulding that fills the port's mouth, with a thin waisted saddle rising off it and a plate across the saddle's end to pull it out by. An OCCUPANT of the aperture it plugs (std/mpo@2 and anything composing it), so it comes out, swaps for a plug, or leaves the port empty. THE ONLY ONE OF THE FOUR CAPS THAT IS NEW: the MPO adapters never drew a cap, so this is read off FS's own product renders rather than moved off an adapter, and every figure it carries is an estimate or a declared modelling choice - see `size-notes` and `provenance.depth`. `common/` for the reason common/lc-boot@1 gives: no standard governs a cap's shape, only the interface it plugs.
components.name: mpo-dust-cap
components.size-notes: THE PIXEL SPANS ARE MEASURED; WHAT THEY ARE A READING OF IS AN INTERPRETATION, NOT SETTLED, which is why both axes say `estimated` and not `photo-measured`. FS's face-on renders of SKU 35510 (the 12x MTP adapter panel) show all twelve ports CAPPED, and nothing in them draws a line between the cap's own outline and the mouth of the aperture it stands in. The panel mounts its adapters PORTRAIT, so the render's vertical reading is this part's width and its horizontal reading is its height. ORTHOGRAPHIC FIRST, because a reading off a perspective render is worth nothing whatever it is a reading of. The six ports of the lower row fit a straight line at a pitch of 81.850 px with a largest residual of 0.68 px - under 1% of the pitch - and a least-squares quadratic term of -0.036 px per index squared, which over the whole row is under a pixel. Both rows read the same size to the pixel (74-75 px by 46-47 px, twelve ports), which a perspective view of a 35 mm-tall plate could not give. Nothing here is fitted to a curve because there is no curve to fit. THE SCALE IS THE RENDER'S OWN PRINTED DIMENSION: the plate spans 633 px against its printed 4.29 in (108.97 mm), 5.809 px/mm, cross-checked on the printed 1.38 in height (35.05 mm), which reads 205 px, 5.848 px/mm - the two 0.67% apart. THE SPANS: each port's content measures 74.5 px on the long axis (74-75 across all twelve, both rows, on two renders of the same panel) and 47 px on the short (46-47), which at 5.809 px/mm is 12.82 and 8.09. Inside that sits a brighter block of 59 by 21 px, 10.16 by 3.62. WHICH OF THE TWO THE CAP IS. That the bright block is the WHOLE cap, sitting in a mouth the 12.82 x 8.09 content outlines, is EXCLUDED: a cap 3.62 on its short axis cannot seal an opening std/mpo@2 gives as 8.0, and the oblique renders show a saddle standing off every port, which is what a bright block in the middle of a port looks like seen end-on. So the content is read as the cap's face. IT IS CLOSE TO THE CORRECTED MOUTH, AND THAT AGREEMENT IS PARTLY BY CONSTRUCTION, so it is not evidence for this reading: this same 12.82 x 8.09 is one of the readings that chose the upper end of the clearance std/mpo@2 was derived with (the way standards.yaml's `mpo-plug` note says its own agreement with `mpo-adapter` is by construction). Axis by axis it does not even match: 0.08 inside std/mpo@2's 12.9 on the long axis and 0.09 over its 8.0 on the short. WHAT IS NOT EXCLUDED is that some of the 12.82 x 8.09 is the mouth's own bevel rather than the cap; if a drawing ever settles the cap, this part gets smaller and not larger.

components.description: Flanged MPO/MTP bulkhead adapter carrying 12 fibres - a black flange held by two screws, a raised housing, and a keyed opening - as FS fits to the back of its FHD MTP cassettes. The opening is an `mpo` slot: an MPO cap or plug seats in it, in front of the housing. Not common/mpo-adapter@2, which is one opening tile in FS's continuous MTP adapter panel and has no flange of its own.
components.name: mpo-flange-adapter
components.size-notes: Read across the width of FS's rear render of SKU 57016 (57016.D.jpg), scaled on the 108.97 mm faceplate that overhangs the cassette body (627 px, 5.75 px/mm). The render is shot from above the cassette, which foreshortens its height and not its width, so the widths are readings and the heights are not. The flange runs about 4.1 to 32.3 on the body, 28.2 across, and is taken as 30.0 to include its chamfered ends. The two screws sit about 24 apart - close to the 25.0 flange hole pattern the `mpo-adapter` registry entry records off US Conec's C9857 drawing - so they are placed 25.0 apart on the part's centre. The 11.0 height is proportion on an estimated cassette back, not a reading.

components.description: Panel-mount MTP-16 adapter - one opening in a bezel, as fitted to FS's FHD 12x MTP-16 adapter panel (SKU 382885). The same tile as common/mpo-adapter@2 in outline and opening, because US Conec states the 16-fibre MT ferrule keeps the traditional MT's external footprint; what differs is sixteen fibre positions on the ferrule row and a key offset from the centre, which stops an MTP-16 plug mating with standard MPO hardware - so the opening it composes is std/mpo16@1, presenting interface mpo16, not std/mpo@2.
components.name: mpo16-adapter
components.size-notes: BORROWED WHOLE from common/mpo-adapter@2, the MPO-8/12/24 tile on FS's 12x MTP panel (35510). FS's adapter-panels datasheet draws its MTP panels as one family - "Type A and Type B MTP adapter panels are of the same dimensions" - and its face-on render of the MTP-16 panel (382885.p3) puts the openings on the pitch it puts the 35510 openings on (13.34 against 13.33 before the frame correction the MTP-12 panel's drawing supplies). US Conec's MTP-16 handout (SM-0022-0823) says the 16-fibre ferrule has the same external footprint as the traditional MT ferrule. So nothing here is a second reading of the tile; see mpo-adapter@2 for where its 13.8 x 9.4 came from.

components.description: The grey dust cap FS ships in each opening of its FHD 12x MTP-16 adapter panel (SKU 382885) - common/mpo-dust-cap@2's shape, mating the MTP-16 interface. FS draws the two caps alike; whether its MTP-16 cap is keyed differently is not visible at the renders' resolution.

components.description: The pull handle of a Type 2 QSFP-DD module - the long-nosed module, whose handle is shorter than a Type 1 handle because the case extends further out of the cage. A closed loop as wide as the module: two arms along the side edges, a grip plate across the far end, and a tall post at each arm root against the nose front, with the arm stepping up from the post to a flat strap level with the top of the nose. Open in the middle, so the fibre connector passes through. No speed lettering: the generic that composes it carries no rate.
components.name: qsfp-dd-pull-tab-type2

components.description: QSFP orthographic views transcribed from a vendor mechanical drawing - top, side and bottom at true scale. A drawing study rather than a placeable part: it exists so the 2D can be checked against the dimensions before any 3D is built from it.

components.description: QSFP port lane LED strip - four triangles, one per lane (no separate link/activity LEDs on this platform)

components.description: QSFP / QSFP-DD pull tab - the flat paddle bail that wraps the module and extends forward, with an elongated opening through it for a finger. Built as a flat loop, two side rails and a front crossbar, rather than a round bail, which is what a tube primitive would give. Vendors colour-code it by reach.
components.name: qsfp-pull-tab

components.description: QSFP / QSFP-DD pull tab, as the part is: a flat U-loop whose two thin arms run forward along the module's side edges and join in a wider grip at the far end, open in the middle so the fibre connector passes through. The grip straddles the module's top edge, its top 1.23 above it, inside the MSA's 3.4 MAX allowance above the module. Each arm roots in a riser block, a tall square post moulded with the strap that stands against the nose front at the module's side edge, 7.5 long and 7.8 tall from the strap top. The strap is S-bent in side view: it leaves the riser 0.47 above the module top, dips 1.5 below that mid-span and rises to the grip, 0.76 above where it left. Each arm is drawn as six boxes stepping along that curve. No speed lettering: the generic that composes it carries no rate.
components.name: qsfp-pull-tab

components.description: QSFP transceiver with a white pull-latch bail, drawn from a vendor mechanical drawing. The face is the module envelope that enters the cage; the bail is a U-bail standing proud of it, and the body carries the heatsink ribs on top and the label area underneath.

components.description: Panel-mount SC duplex adapter, as fitted to an FS FHD SC panel - one body carrying two SC ports STACKED vertically, not side by side, on the 12.7 SC duplex pitch. A blue frame standing proud of the plate, each port a real SC opening (std/sc-bore@1). The black dust caps FS ships are occupants of the openings, not part of this adapter: each opening ships holding common/sc-dust-cap@1, its `default:` (provenance.shipped-caps). Distinct from common/lc-duplex-adapter, whose pair sits abreast, and from common/sc-apc, which is a device-specific moulded PON bay rather than a panel adapter.
components.name: sc-duplex-adapter
components.size-notes: 9.4 is the width v1 measured: six bodies 9.32 to 9.49 on FS's face-on render of SKU 57058. 25.4 is the height, and v1's 12.0 was the defect this major exists for - two 9.0 SC openings cannot stack in 12.0. On 57058.main.jpg, scaled on the 108.97 mm plate (80-719 px, 5.86 px/mm), every adapter's blue frame runs from y 370 to 518, 149 px, 25.4 mm. It is corroborated twice: 25.4 is exactly two cells on the 12.7 SC duplex pitch, and Molex's SC duplex adapter (106167) is drawn 9.4 wide and 25.9 overall. No depth in `size`: how far the frame stands out of the plate is `relief`, not an aperture.

components.description: The black dust cap FS ships in an FHD SC port - 8.8 x 11.45, with a lighter raised grip across its middle for finger and thumb. An OCCUPANT of the opening it plugs (std/sc-bore@1 and anything composing it), so it comes out, swaps for a plug, or leaves the port empty. It was drawn as part of common/sc-duplex-adapter until @3 took it off; its figures move here unchanged. `common/` for the reason common/lc-boot@1 gives: no standard governs a cap's shape, only the interface it plugs.
components.name: sc-dust-cap

components.description: Panel-mount SC simplex adapter - one flangeless body carrying one SC port, a real SC opening (std/sc-bore@1) with its key slot to the LEFT when unrotated. components.size-notes: 9.4 x 12.8 is the adapter body SENKO's SC Premium Adapter drawing prints (DS-SC-000010 Rev A, front view: `9.4 -0.2` and `12.8 +/-0.2`), the body standards.yaml's `sc-simplex-receptacle` entry records beside the 7.5 x 9.0 opening it surrounds. components.description: The printed strip beside an Eaton Rack PDU G4 outlet section - a band in the section's colour with a dark window under each of its seven outlets carrying the outlet's number. The colour and the seven numbers are fields; the strip is one drawing for every section.
components.name: g4-outlet-labels

components.description: The outlet status lamp of an Eaton Rack PDU G4 that meters or switches each outlet - a small clear dome on the edge of the outlet moulding, one at the far end of every outlet, lit green while the outlet is powered and red while it is off. Placed beside its outlet and bound to it with `for:`.
components.name: g4-outlet-led

components.description: The digital load meter of a 1U Eaton Tripp Lite series switched PDU - a two-digit green seven-segment readout of the total output load in amps, in a black window with a thin bezel and no button.
components.name: tripplite-ammeter

components.description: The fixed input cord of a 1U Eaton Tripp Lite series 20 A PDU - 12 ft of cord ending in a NEMA L5-20P locking plug, leaving the rear face through a black strain-relief bushing with a round top and a square collar. Drawn as the rear face shows it; the cord and plug beyond it are not.
components.name: tripplite-cord-l5-20p

components.description: The round lamp window of an Eaton Tripp Lite series rack PDU face - a flush grey window about 6 mm across, one beside every switched outlet and one for the LX network interface's status. A lamp knows only that it is lit or not; what lit means, and in what colour, is the placement's statement.
components.name: tripplite-led

components.description: The digital load meter of an Eaton Tripp Lite series 20 A rack PDU - a two-digit green seven-segment readout of the load in amps, printed LOAD (AMPS) above it upside down and below it upright so it reads either way up, with the round Select / Rotate push button beside it.
components.name: tripplite-load-meter

components.description: The toolless mounting button on the back of an Eaton Tripp Lite series zero-U PDU - a black head 17.67 across on a short shaft, screwed through a round base plate, that drops into a rack's button-mount slot and slides down into the slot's narrow end. Seen here from behind the PDU.
components.name: tripplite-mounting-button

components.description: The Eaton Tripp Lite series WEBCARDLX network card as a 1U Tripp Lite PDU carries it, behind its own black faceplate: a 10/100 Ethernet port with its link and speed lamps, a recessed reset button under it, a micro-USB console port, a USB-A port for EnviroSense2 sensors and a status lamp. The faceplate is a plate with a screw tab at its lower left and its upper right.

mgmt.mixed: the card's service connections - the 10/100 Ethernet port, the micro-USB console and the USB-A sensor port

components.name: webcardlx

components.description: Hot-swappable fan module for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB). Five across the rear in a 4+1 redundant arrangement, numbered FAN 0 at the right to FAN 4 at the left. Two counter-rotating rotors in tandem behind a circular honeycomb finger guard, with a red D-handle on the left of the faceplate.
components.name: agr-fan

components.description: Removable bottom air filter for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB). A dark metal frame with open sections and reticulated foam behind them. It bolts onto the OUTSIDE of the faceplate with captive thumb screws - it does not slide into a bay - so it is placed, not seated. A plain rectangle, wider than the top filter because it also spans the SFP28 pair.
components.name: agr-filter-bottom

components.description: Removable top air filter for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB). NOT the AGR420's: that chassis measured this part and rejected it - 353.5 mm against the 417 its front needs, and stepped for the AGR400's TWO QSFP-DD blocks where the AGR420 front has one. The AGR420 draws edgecore/agr420-filter-top@1 with agr420-filter-step@1 instead. A dark metal frame with open sections and reticulated foam behind them. It bolts onto the OUTSIDE of the faceplate with captive thumb screws - it does not slide into a bay - so it is placed, not seated. Its outline is not a plain rectangle - it drops deeper over each QSFP-DD block, which the maintainer describes as two nubs and the photographs confirm.
components.name: agr-filter-top

components.description: Chassis grounding landing on the AGR400/AGR420 rear, between the PSU bay and the fans. An IEC 60417-5019 earth symbol above a two-hole plate for a two-hole grounding lug.
components.name: agr-ground-plate

components.description: Caution label near the rear left of the top cover on the Edgecore AGR400 / AGR420.
components.name: agr-label-caution

components.description: Serial number, SKU and MAC label on the top cover on the Edgecore AGR400 / AGR420.
components.name: agr-label-serial

components.description: Regulatory and specification label on the top cover on the Edgecore AGR400 / AGR420.
components.name: agr-label-spec

components.description: Captive slotted thumb screw at each corner of the Edgecore AGR400 / AGR420 front panel, holding the rack flange to the chassis. A bright plated head about 8.4 mm across with a single broad slot, standing proud of the paint. Much larger than common/screw-head, which is 3.6 mm and reads as a machine screw rather than a thumb screw at this scale.
components.name: agr-panel-screw

components.description: AC-DC hot-swappable PSU for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB). Same shell as the DC unit with an IEC C14 appliance inlet in place of the terminal block.
components.name: agr-psu-ac

attrs.input: -40 to -75 VDC, 40 A max per PSU

components.description: DC-DC hot-swappable PSU for the Edgecore AGR400 (AS7946-30XB) and AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB). Black bail handle on the left, a two-post -48 V terminal block in the middle and a red latch on the right. This is the unit we photographed.
components.name: agr-psu-dc

components.description: Removable BOTTOM air filter for the Edgecore AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB) - the full-width band of it. The mirror of the top filter and shorter, stopping at panel x 412 rather than running under the management corner. The same physical filter also carries a deeper section beside the QSFP-DD column, which is agr420-filter-step.
components.name: agr420-filter-bottom

components.description: The deep section of an Edgecore AGR420 air filter, beside the QSFP-DD column at the left of the front panel, where the nearest port row is 17 mm away and the frame can drop a second foam cell in. Both the top and the bottom filter carry one; it is not a separate FRU, it is the stepped end of one, split out because a placement is a bounding rectangle.
components.name: agr420-filter-step

components.description: Removable TOP air filter for the Edgecore AGR420 (AS7946-74XKSB) - the full-width band of it. A dark metal frame with open sections and reticulated foam behind them, bolted onto the OUTSIDE of the faceplate with two captive thumb screws; it does not slide into a bay, so it is placed, not seated. The same physical filter also carries a deeper section beside the QSFP-DD column, which is agr420-filter-step.
components.name: agr420-filter-top

components.description: The 2000 W AC power supply of the Edgecore AGR560 (AS9947-36XKB), sold as the FRU PS-2202-8L - a 73.5 x 40 CRPS shell carrying a Lite-On fan at the left with its rating printed on the rotor hub, an IEC 60320 C14 inlet at the right, a pull handle across the foot of the fan guard and the release latch on the right edge. NOT the AIS800-64D's supply: that one is 3000 W on a C20 inlet in a 36 mm guard, and this is 2000 W on a C14 in a 41.9 mm guard. The two share a bay size and nothing else.
components.name: agr560-psu-ac

components.description: The 2000 W -48 VDC power supply of the Edgecore AGR560 (AS9947-36XKB), sold as the FRU DD-2202-1L - the AC unit's 73.5 x 40 shell and Lite-On fan with a TWO-STUD terminal block where that one has a C14 inlet. Two studs, not the six of the AIS800-64D's DC supply: this machine is half the power and its cable is #6 AWG where that one's is #4.
components.name: agr560-psu-dc

components.description: The 3000 W AC power supply of the Edgecore AIS800-64D and AIS800-64O - a CRPS-form module in a bright housing with an octagonal wire fan guard at its left, a black pull loop hanging under the guard, an IEC C20 inlet standing on its side at the right and a coloured release latch down the inlet's right edge. Two stack one above the other at the left of the rear. NOT the 32-port models' supply: that one is 53.7 wide with a Saf-D-Grid; this one is 73.5 wide and the datasheet names the inlet "IEC 60320 C20".
components.name: ais800-64-psu-ac

components.description: The 3000 W DC power supply of the Edgecore AIS800-64D and AIS800-64O - the AC unit's 73.5 x 40 CRPS shell with a six-stud terminal block in place of the fan guard and inlet: two rows of three M-studs under a lifting cover, honeycomb fields either side, a black pull loop standing at the left and the coloured release latch at the right. Drawn from the quick start guide's own Connect Power figure of this face.
components.name: ais800-64-psu-dc

components.description: A rear fan module of the Edgecore AIS800-32D and AIS800-32O - a honeycomb-grilled black tray with a large coloured U-bail across its lower half and one unlabelled lamp at its top left. SEVEN fill this chassis in a 6+1 arrangement, which is one more bay than any other tray in this library's Edgecore rears, and at 41.65 mm it is the narrowest of them.
components.name: ais800-fan

components.description: The 2400 W AC power supply of the Edgecore AIS800-32D and AIS800-32O - a bright CRPS-style module with a latticed grille across its left half, a coloured U-bail hinged down its left edge, one unlabelled lamp at its top left corner, an Anderson Saf-D-Grid appliance inlet standing upright at its right and a small release tab at the bottom right. NOT an IEC inlet: 2400 W on a 200 V line is 12 A continuous and the vendor names the connector outright.
components.name: ais800-psu-ac

components.description: The 2400 W DC power supply of the Edgecore AIS800-32D and AIS800-32O - a bright CRPS-style module with a coloured bail stowed across its top, a ground stud at its top left, a two-pole screw-down barrier block silkscreened -40 - -72 and RTN across its middle, a latticed grille and one unlabelled lamp at its right, and a small release tab at the bottom right. It shares the AIS800's bay with edgecore/ais800-psu-ac@1 and shares none of that module's face.
components.name: ais800-psu-dc

components.description: The Edgecore AMX3200's 1200 W DC supply, ordered as AMX-3200-48V-PSU - a 73.5 x 40.0 module with its release latch at the left edge, its three-pin DC terminal block beside it, its own fan behind a guard at the right, and a black U-handle under the fan. Two seat at the ends of the rear, PSU2 at the left and PSU1 at the right.
components.name: amx-3200-48v-psu

components.description: The Edgecore AMX3200's 1200 W AC supply, ordered as AMX-3200-AC-PSU - a 73.5 x 40.0 module with its release latch at the left edge, its IEC C14 inlet beside it, its own fan behind a guard at the right, and a black U-handle under the fan. Two seat at the ends of the rear, PSU2 at the left and PSU1 at the right.
components.name: amx-3200-ac-psu

components.description: The Edgecore AMX3200's rear fan tray, ordered as AMX-3200-FAN - a 42.2 x 39.7 module, honeycomb across its face over one 40.5 mm fan, with a red handle swept across its middle and a small lens at its top left. FIVE fill the rear in a 4+1 redundancy, numbered 5 to 1 from left to right.
components.name: amx-3200-fan

components.description: The blank cover panel for an unused AMX3200 sled slot - shipped one to a box ('1 x Blank cover panel accessory') and required by the guide over any slot without a sled.

components.description: The Edgecore AMX3200's interface sled, ordered as AMX-3200-SLED400 - a 183.8 x 41.9 front module carrying two 400G CFP2-DCO line ports and eight 100G QSFP28 client ports, a honeycomb vent over the CFP2 cages, and a lever along its foot that locks it into the chassis. components.description: The Edgecore COR550's rear fan tray - a 68.0 x 62.3 module, honeycomb across its whole face with one rotor showing through the mesh, and a narrow red D-handle standing on its INBOARD edge rather than sweeping across the face the way this vendor's 2RU trays usually do. FIVE fill the chassis in a 4+1 redundancy, numbered FAN 0 at the outboard end and FAN 4 beside the supplies, which is right to left across the rear elevation.
components.name: cor550-fan

components.description: The Edgecore COR550's per-port QSFP28 lamp group - THREE round lamps in a row on a 2.70 mm pitch, sitting in the white legend strip that runs between the two ports of a column. Each 100G port has its own group; the top port's sits left of the column centre and the bottom port's right of it, which is why one strip carries twelve lamps across a four-port block.
components.name: cor550-lane-leds

components.description: The hot-swappable AC supply of the Edgecore COR550 - a 54.5 x 40.8 module in the common CRPS envelope, its own fan behind a honeycomb vent at the inboard end, a black D-handle laid across that vent, an IEC 60320 C14 inlet standing on end at the outboard end, and a red release latch beside it. TWO stack in one column at the left of the rear face, PSU1 above PSU0. Named for the chassis because no staged COR550 document prints an ordering code for the supply; see `the-name-is-the-chassis-because-no-document-names-the-fru`.
components.name: cor550-psu-ac

components.description: The fan tray of the Edgecore CSR310 (AS7315-27X) - a hot-swappable 1RU tray at the right-hand end of the faceplate carrying the chassis's redundant fan modules, with a grab handle across its top and a captive knurled thumbscrew at its foot. Edgecore part FAN-1U-1x1J-S. The airflow direction is printed on its face as an arrow.
components.name: csr310-fan-tray

components.description: The AC power supply of the Edgecore CSR310 (AS7315-27X) - the same hot-swappable 1RU half-height module as the DC unit with an IEC C14 inlet in place of the terminal block, marked N / earth / L beneath it. Edgecore part SPAACTN-03BG.
components.name: csr310-psu-ac

components.description: The -48 VDC power supply of the Edgecore CSR310 (AS7315-27X) - a hot-swappable 1RU half-height module landing its feed on a three-pole barrier terminal block, with a pull handle down the right-hand edge and a latch at its foot. Edgecore part CRXT-T0T12BS; the quick start calls the bare unit CRXT-T0T12B and says only that part will fit.
components.name: csr310-psu-dc

components.description: A rear fan module of the Edgecore CSR440 (AS7535-28XB) - a honeycomb-grilled tray with the fan visible through it, a red pull handle across the foot, a captive thumbscrew above its bay number, and an airflow arrow beside that number. Six of them fill the rear panel.
components.name: csr440-fan

components.description: The AC power supply of the Edgecore CSR440 (AS7535-28XB) - a hot-swappable CRPS-style module in a bright housing, with a C14 inlet TURNED ON ITS SIDE at the left, a wire bail handle across the middle, a perforated exhaust field on the right and a coloured release latch at the top. Nothing like the dark terminal-block supply of the CSR310 and CSR430, which is why it is its own part.
components.name: csr440-psu-ac

components.description: A rear fan module of the Edgecore DCS201 (AS5835-54X) - a honeycomb-grilled tray with a pull bar across its foot and a diamond airflow legend in its upper right corner. WIDER THAN THE 48.6 mm common/fan-module THE REST OF THIS FAMILY SEATS, and there are five of them rather than six, which is why it is its own part.
components.name: dcs201-fan

components.description: The 400 W AC power supply of the Edgecore DCS201 (AS5835-54X) - a CRPS-style module in a bright housing with a square-latticed exhaust grille at the left, a wire bail handle over it, an IEC C14 inlet turned on its side at the right and a coloured release latch at its foot. The same 54 x 40 face the rest of this family uses; a DIFFERENT RATING, which is why it is not common/psu-ac-650@3.
components.name: dcs201-psu-ac

components.description: The 400 W -48 VDC power supply of the Edgecore DCS201 (AS5835-54X) - the same 54 x 40 CRPS face as the AC supply, with a THREE-POLE PLUGGABLE GREEN TERMINAL in place of the C14 inlet. The quick start wires it DC return, -36 to -75 VDC, Ground.
components.name: dcs201-psu-dc

components.description: A rear fan module of the Edgecore DCS240 (AS9726-32DB) - a honeycomb-grilled tray with a single large rotor visible behind the mesh and a coloured pull bar ACROSS ITS MIDDLE rather than at its foot. Six of them fill this chassis where the DCS201's shell takes five, and they are narrower: 48.5 mm against 58.8.
components.name: dcs240-fan

components.description: The AC power supply of the Edgecore DCS240 (AS9726-32DB) - a CRPS-style module in a bright housing with a latticed exhaust grille at the left, a wire bail handle over it, an IEC C14 inlet turned on its side at the right and a coloured release latch down its right edge. Rated 1000 W at 110 V and 1500 W at 230 V, which is why it is not any 650 W or 400 W part in this library.
components.name: dcs240-psu-ac

components.description: The -48 VDC power supply of the Edgecore DCS240 (AS9726-32DB) - the same 54.4 x 40 CRPS face as the AC variant with a DC terminal in place of the C14 inlet. Rated 1600 W.
components.name: dcs240-psu-dc

components.description: The Edgecore DCS500's rear fan tray - a 63.0 x 62.6 module, honeycomb across the face over one rotor, with a red D-handle on its RIGHT edge. FOUR fill the chassis between the two supplies in a 3+1 redundancy.
components.name: dcs500-fan

components.description: The Edgecore DCS500's per-port QSFP28 lamp row - FOUR round lamps in a line on a 4.30 mm pitch, printed on the faceplate outside the cage, above a top-row port and below a bottom-row one. One lamp per breakout lane, as the vendor states.
components.name: dcs500-lane-leds

components.description: The 850 W AC supply of the Edgecore DCS500 - a 50.9 x 39.4 bright-housed module with a square-cell exhaust lattice, an IEC C14 inlet at its left end, a black handle standing up its middle and a red release latch at its right end. Two seat in the rear's lower corners, one either side of the fan trays.
components.name: dcs500-psu-ac

components.description: The hot-swappable fan tray of the Edgecore DCS520 (AS9736-64D) - an 80.1 x 83.5 honeycomb face with a red pull bar lying at a slight angle across it, a release button at the bar's centre and a status lamp at the top left. Four of them fill the middle of the rear between the two supplies. IT LOOKS LIKE THE AIS800 FAMILY'S 2RU TRAY AND THIS FILE DOES NOT CLAIM TO BE IT - see the provenance.
components.name: dcs520-fan

attrs.input-note: Anderson Saf-D-Grid; also rated for 240 VDC HVDC

components.description: The 2400 W AC/HVDC power supply of the Edgecore DCS520 (AS9736-64D) - a TALL, NARROW 39.7 x 53.3 module, not the 73.5 x 40 CRPS brick the rest of this 2RU shell family carries, because this machine stands one supply at each END of its rear with the four fan trays between them. An Anderson Saf-D-Grid inlet fills the lower half, a wire-guard vent the upper, and a black pull handle lies diagonally across the vent. THE TWO SUPPLIES ARE THE SAME PART MOUNTED ONE UP AND ONE DOWN, which the guide states.
components.name: dcs520-psu-ac

components.description: One of the three FIXED fans on the rear of the Edgecore EPS121 and EPS122 (AS4625-54T and AS4625-54P) - a 25.5 x 15.9 guard with a spoked rotor behind it. NOT A FRU: both documents say "2+1 fixed redundant fans", the guide's FRU Replacement section covers the supplies only, and there is no bay, no latch and no handle to draw. It is placed, not bayed, and that is the whole point of the distinction.
components.name: eps-fan-fixed

components.description: The hot-swappable AC power supply of the Edgecore EPS121 (AS4625-54T) - a 50.4 x 38.7 module with a perforated intake, a red U-handle, a red release latch and an IEC inlet. NOT the EPS122's supply: that one is 62.3 wide, carries its own fan and is rated three times the input current.
components.name: eps-psu-ac

components.description: The hot-swappable AC power supply of the Edgecore EPS122 (AS4625-54P) - a 62.3 x 39.9 module carrying its own fan behind the face, a perforated intake, a red U-handle, a red release latch and an IEC inlet. Twelve millimetres wider than the EPS121's supply and rated three times its input current, because this machine feeds a PoE budget of up to 1920 W.
components.name: eps-psu-poe

components.description: One of the three FIXED fans on the rear of the Edgecore EPS112 (AS4625-30P) - a round 25.1 mm guard with a five-bladed rotor behind it, set straight into the rear panel with no tray, no latch and no handle. NOT A FRU: the datasheet and the guide both say "fixed 2+1 redundant fans", and the guide's FRU Replacement section covers the supplies only. It is PLACED, not bayed.
components.name: eps112-fan-fixed

components.description: The hot-swappable 600 W AC power supply of the Edgecore EPS112 (AS4625-30P) - a 73.2 x 40.2 module with a red C-handle at the inboard end, its own fan behind the face, DC OK and AC OK lamps, an IEC 60320 C14 inlet and a red release latch on the outboard edge. Ordered as UP6001R-1079G.
components.name: eps112-psu-ac

components.description: The hot-swappable fan tray of the Edgecore EPS200 series - a 47.5 x 39.5 module with a honeycomb face, one rotor behind it, a captive thumbscrew and a coloured pull bar that runs nearly the full width of the tray. Ordered as FAN-1U-1x1M, and the SAME PART IN ALL THREE CHASSIS: the ordering tables of the EPS201, EPS202 and EPS203 each list it as "Fan Module ... (for EPS201/AS4630-54TE, EPS202/AS4630-54PE, EPS203/AS4630-54NPE)". Named for the FRU rather than for one of the three that seat it.
components.name: eps200-fan-tray

components.description: The hot-swappable 1200 W AC supply of the Edgecore EPS202 and EPS203 - a 72.0 x 39.5 module with its own fan behind the face, a release latch and an IEC 60320 C14 inlet with a cord retainer. Ordered as YPEB1200AM-1A03P10 and named for that FRU rather than for either chassis that seats it; the EPS201 on the same shell takes a 150 W supply instead.
components.name: eps200-psu-1200w

components.description: The hot-swappable 150 W AC supply of the Edgecore EPS201 - a 51.3 x 39.5 module with a coloured release latch at the inboard edge, a perforated intake, a recessed pull slot and an IEC 60320 C14 inlet with a cord retainer. Ordered as YM-1151D, in two airflows: A03R front-to-rear and A02R back-to-front. Twenty-one millimetres narrower than the 1200 W supply its EPS202 and EPS203 shell-mates take, which is what eight times the output costs in sheet metal.
components.name: eps201-psu-150w

components.description: A rear fan module of the Edgecore EXP800-16O - a honeycomb-grilled tray with a single rotor behind the mesh and a coloured pull bar across its middle stamped F2B. Six fill this chassis. It is NARROWER than the rest of this line's trays, 41.45 mm against the DCS240's 48.5 and the DCS201's 58.8, because the bays here are separated by a 7.5 mm chassis rail rather than butting against one another.
components.name: exp800-fan

components.description: The AC power supply of the Edgecore EXP800-16O - a CRPS-style module in a bright housing with a latticed exhaust grille, a wire bail handle over it, an IEC C14 inlet turned on its side at the right, and a coloured release latch DOWN ITS LEFT EDGE rather than its right. Narrower than the rest of this line's supplies at 50.6 mm.
components.name: exp800-psu-ac

components.description: Edgecore's FAN-2U-1x1SN rear fan tray - a near-square 2RU tray, honeycomb across its whole face, one 80 mm rotor showing through the mesh, a wide coloured pull bar sweeping across its middle with the release button set into the bar, and one unlabelled lens at its top left. FOUR fill a chassis, each carrying TWO fans in series behind one grille, which is why the vendor's "8 fans total with 7+1 redundancy" counts twice what this library's bays do. It is not one machine's part - the AIS800-64D, the AIS800-64O and the AGR560 all seat this same tray on the same 440 x 649.2 x 87 shell - which is why it is named for the FRU their three datasheets print rather than for any one of them.
components.name: fan-2u-1x1sn

components.description: The air-filter slot cover on the AS5915 cell-site gateways - the blanking plate that ships in the filter bay at the left-hand end of the faceplate, retained by two captive slotted thumbscrews. Removing it is step 1 of the quick start's optional air-filter procedure; the filter assembly slides into the same opening.
components.name: filter-slot-5915

components.description: The air-filter slot cover on the AS5915-16X - the blanking plate in the filter bay at the left-hand end of the faceplate, retained by two captive cross-head screws. The AS5915-18X's plate is a different size with different screws and is edgecore/filter-slot-5915@1; this one is narrower and does not reach the panel edge.
components.name: filter-slot-5915-16x

components.description: FS FHD-1MTP6SCDOS2A - MTP-12 (male) to six SC duplex, 12 fibres, OS2, Type A polarity. FS SKU 57058. The first component in this library to compose common/sc-duplex-adapter@5.
components.name: fhd-1mtp12-sc-os2-a
components.size-notes: The faceplate is MEASURED off FS's face-on render of SKU 57058 (57058.main.jpg), scaled on the 108.97 mm FHD module width and validated against the 35.05 mm height to 0.57% - independently reproducing the exact scale check already recorded in standards.yaml's sc-duplex-adapter entry, since this is the same image the adapter body width was measured from. Corroborated by FS's own dimension line on 57058.B.jpg, which reads 4.29in x 1.38in - exactly 108.97 x 35.05, the same reading 57016.B.jpg gives for the LC cassette, confirming both share one FHD faceplate. THE DEPTH IS THE LC CASSETTE'S TOO. 57058.B.jpg's own depth line reads 4.64in, 117.86 mm. Until this contract's 1.5.2 this paragraph set that against a 4.34in on 57016.B.jpg and called the SC body 7.62 mm deeper, with an SC adapter's proud ferrule and shutter offered as the reason. The 4.34in was a misreading: 57016.B.jpg reads 4.64in as well, and fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@4 now carries 117.86. There was never a difference to explain, and a physical reason was found for it anyway - which is the thing worth remembering about this paragraph.

components.description: The back of FS FHD-1MTP6SCDOS2A (SKU 57058): the cassette body seen from behind, carrying its single MTP-12 trunk adapter.
components.name: fhd-1mtp12-sc-rear
components.size-notes:
NOT MEASURED, AND NOT MEASURABLE FROM WHAT IS HELD - the identical situation fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-rear@3 already documents for SKU 57016, and the same numbers are reused rather than re-guessed, for a reason stronger than "the family shares a rear": 57058.D.jpg is the only rear view held here too, it is the same top-rear three-quarter composition, and panel_measure refuses it at 3.7694450%, the SAME figure (independently reproduced) that 57016.D.jpg gives - to four significant figures, not just "close". Two independent SKUs' rear renders failing panel_measure's own scale-validity check by the identical percentage is strong evidence they were shot from the same rig against the same physical rear tooling, which is exactly what 99.0 x 31.0 already assumes. It still cannot be scaled on the faceplate, because the faceplate OVERHANGS the body - the rear face is the body, and the body is narrower by an amount nobody has measured. 99.0 x 31.0 is proportion read off that render against the known 108.97 x 35.05 front, carried over from fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-rear@3 rather than re-derived. A face-on photograph of the back settles it for either SKU.
NO DEPTH IS DECLARED, AND THAT IS THE READING. This contract is a FACE - the drawing of a back, not a part with a back of its own - and render.py turns a `size.d` on a fixed component into `data-depth`, an aperture as big as the whole face. The kit then builds THAT pit and drops the recesses inside it, because it takes only the innermost cavity of a nest: the estimated `d: 2.0` carried until now swallowed the recesses composed onto this face, so a bulkhead's mouth was not built at all and the whole back sat 2 mm below the cassette's edge in 3D. The depth of the body this face closes belongs to the cassette that carries it - `body.depth` there - and differs between them.

components.size-notes: The faceplate is MEASURED off FS's face-on render of SKU 57016, scaled on the 108.97 mm FHD module width and validated against the 35.05 mm height to 1.02% - and corroborated independently by FS's own dimension line on 57016.B.jpg, which reads 4.29in x 1.38in, exactly 108.97 x 35.05. The 117.86 depth is the 4.64in on that same dimension line. THIS DEPTH WAS 110.24 UNTIL 2.0.0, A MISREADING OF THAT LINE AS 4.34in. Read at five times, 57016.B.jpg's depth figure is 4.64in, and nothing in the image supports a 3 in that place. The wrong figure made this cassette 7.62 mm shallower than fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-af@3 and fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-u@3, which are the same body with the fibres crossed differently behind it, and whose 117.86 comes from a different source: FS's product pages for 57037 and 182641, each stating 35 x 109 x 118 mm (1.38 x 4.29 x 4.64 in). This contract is a FACE - the drawing of a back, not a part with a back of its own - and render.py turns a `size.d` on a fixed component into `data-depth`, an aperture as big as the whole face. components.description: FS FHD Fiber Splice Cassette, LC UPC, OS2, 12 Fibers. FS SKU 382907. Twelve trunk fibres fusion-spliced inside the cassette to six LC duplex adapters on the front - one of eleven splice cassettes in FS's FHD catalogue, and the only one this library models.
components.name: fhd-splice-12-lc
components.size-notes: NO IMAGE OF THIS PART EXISTS. No photograph in working/intake/fs/fhd/photos shows any of the eleven splice cassettes in the catalogue, and no per-SKU datasheet for 382907 was staged - working/intake/fs/fhd/COVERAGE.md records that plainly. 108.97 x 35.05 x 117.86 is BORROWED WHOLE from fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@4 (SKU 57016), whose faceplate and depth are photo-measured and drawing-sourced respectively: every FHD module shares the same 108.97 x 35.05 faceplate by definition of the format (the same reasoning library/devices/fs/fhd-1ufce/device.yaml's own `bays` note gives for sizing an empty bay before any cassette existed to measure), and the 117.86 depth is carried across on the same family-envelope assumption, not a second measurement. IT WAS 110.24 UNTIL 2.0.0 because the source it is borrowed from carried a misreading of FS's dimension line (4.34in for 4.64in); the borrowing was faithful and the figure it copied was not - see fs/fhd-1mtp6lcd-os2-a@4's size-notes. `spec/tools/intake/panel_measure.py` still refuses any scale that fails to reproduce the 35.05 mm height - that is what makes the faceplate a constant rather than a free guess - but nothing in this contract was itself run through it, because there is no image of 382907 to run.

components.description: The back of FS FHD's LC UPC OS2 12-fibre splice cassette (SKU 382907): the cassette body seen from behind, carrying its fusion-splice tray in place of the MTP trunk adapter fhd-1mtp6lcd-rear@3 carries.
components.name: fhd-splice-12-lc-rear
components.size-notes:
NOT MEASURED, AND NOTHING TO MEASURE IT FROM. No photograph of SKU 382907, front or back, is held anywhere in working/intake/fs/fhd/photos - not a three-quarter render, not even a product thumbnail - and no per-SKU datasheet for it was staged (working/intake/fs/fhd/COVERAGE.md records that). 99.0 x 31.0 reuses fhd-1mtp6lcd-rear@3's own figures whole, on the reasoning that every FHD cassette shares one body envelope regardless of what its rear carries - but that source contract is itself marked ESTIMATED throughout (proportion read off a three-quarter render panel_measure refused), not measured, so reusing it here is an estimate built on an estimate and is recorded as `estimated`, not `borrowed`, which this library's vocabulary reserves for reuse of a MEASURED figure. A face-on photograph of this SKU's back, or of any splice cassette's back, settles it.
NO DEPTH IS DECLARED, AND THAT IS THE READING. This contract is a FACE - the drawing of a back, not a part with a back of its own - and render.py turns a `size.d` on a fixed component into `data-depth`, an aperture as big as the whole face. The kit then builds THAT pit and drops the recesses inside it, because it takes only the innermost cavity of a nest: the estimated `d: 2.0` carried until now swallowed the recesses composed onto this face, so a bulkhead's mouth was not built at all and the whole back sat 2 mm below the cassette's edge in 3D. The depth of the body this face closes belongs to the cassette that carries it - `body.depth` there - and differs between them.
