Which module it is - rate, reach, wavelength, watts - is a fact about a vendor product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 5), never here. generic/cfp4-mpo@1 is the same module with the other face.
components.name: cfp4-lc

components.description: A generic CFP4 with one MPO face - the shape of the CFP4 parallel-fibre optic with a twelve-position receptacle, standing for all of them. A narrow body behind a head that is taller than it, one MPO receptacle at the middle, key up and pinned, and a bail whose bar lies across the top of the head because the module is seated. Which module it is - rate, reach, wavelength, watts - is a fact about a vendor product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 5), never here. generic/cfp4-lc@1 is the same module with the other face.
components.name: cfp4-mpo

components.description: A California Standard CS8365C locking plug (50 A 250 V three phase, three pole, four wire), face on: the grip, the face, three curved blades (two with a bent tab) round a grounding rivet. The earth contact is a spring on the metal shell, not a blade. The input plug at the end of a three-phase PDU's cord.
components.name: cs8365c-plug

components.description: A generic optical CXP with one two-row MPO face - the shape of the CXP transceiver with a twenty-four-fibre receptacle, standing for all of them. A short snout that enters the receptacle behind a body that is wider and taller than it and stands wholly outside, one MPO receptacle in the body front, pinned, and a pull tab leaving the top of the body as a loop. Which module it is - rate, lane count, reach, wavelength, watts - is a fact about a vendor product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 5), never here. Not a CXP cable end.
components.name: cxp-mpo

components.description: A DA-15 alarm cable plug: the MALE fifteen-position two-row D-subminiature connector in its backshell hood on its cable, seen from the cable end as a front elevation sees it seated: the hood, the two thumbscrews either side of it and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats on a `da15` panel connector at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the far end of the stub.
components.name: da15-plug
components.size-notes: both figures are the die-cast hood NorComp drawing 979-015-030R121 dimensions, 39.9 across the ears and 15.3 thick at the front; a plastic or moulded hood of the same shell size is a little different

components.description: A DB-25 status cable plug: the MALE twenty-five-position D-subminiature connector in its backshell hood on its cable, seen from the cable end as a front elevation sees it seated: the hood, the two thumbscrews either side of it and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats on a `db25` panel connector at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the far end of the stub.
components.name: db25-plug
components.size-notes: both figures are the die-cast hood NorComp drawing 979-025-030R121 dimensions, 53.5 across the ears and 15.7 thick at the front; a plastic or moulded hood of the same shell size is a little different

components.description: A DE-9 serial or alarm cable plug: the FEMALE nine-position D-subminiature connector in its backshell hood on its cable, seen from the cable end as a front elevation sees it seated: the hood, the two thumbscrews either side of it and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats on a `db9` panel connector at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the far end of the stub.
components.name: db9-plug
components.size-notes: both figures are the die-cast hood NorComp drawing 979-009-030R121 dimensions, 31 across the ears and 15.6 thick at the front; a plastic or moulded hood of the same shell size is a little different

components.description: A DC barrel power plug on its cable, at the common 5.5 mm barrel, seen from the cable end as a front elevation sees it seated: the flange that stops against the jack, the round grip and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats in a `dc-barrel` jack at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the far end of the stub. It is a nominal plug chosen for the library, not the plug of any one device, and it states no voltage and no current.
components.name: dc-barrel-plug
components.size-notes: both figures are the 8.2 diameter of the grip on the Same Sky PP3-002A drawing, a plug chosen to stand for the class; no device that places the jack states the size of its own plug

components.description: A straight 1.0/2.3 crimp plug on a coax cable, seen from the face: the push-pull latch sleeve, the crimp ferrule and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats in a `din-1-0-2-3` jack at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the stub's far end.
components.name: din-1-0-2-3-plug

components.description: A straight F crimp plug on a 75 ohm coax cable, seen from the face: the 7/16 hex coupling nut, the ribbed crimp ferrule and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats in an `f-type` jack at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the stub's far end.
components.name: f-type-plug

components.description: A moulded VGA cable plug: the MALE high-density fifteen-position D-subminiature connector in its moulded hood on its cable, seen from the cable end as a front elevation sees it seated: the hood, the two thumbscrew knobs either side of the strain relief and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats on an `hd15` panel connector at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the far end of the stub.
components.name: hd15-plug
components.size-notes: both figures are printed in a table on one cable data sheet (Legrand S000091720EN-01, p.2), not dimensioned on a drawing; a second moulded plug scales a little smaller

components.description: An LC duplex plug as it is SEATED - the cable end that fills BOTH ports of a duplex LC adapter at once. Two generic/lc-plug@2 bodies held SIDE BY SIDE at the 6.25 duplex pitch by a clip, each turned latch UP, so the pair is drawn on the canonical spanning axis and each half keeps the plug's own compressed latch, rear point and relief. Occupies the `lc-duplex` slot a duplex adapter presents on itself, which is mutually exclusive with its two bore slots.
components.name: lc-duplex-plug

components.description: An LC fibre plug as it is SEATED, front view - the four-tier keyed silhouette of the free plug (provenance.free-state) with its latch compressed into the adapter's keyway, and drawn in the bore's own convention: latch DOWN unrotated, as std/lc-bore@3 and std/lc-bulkhead-bore@1 draw their tongue, so the turn a seat applies carries the latch into the keyway on every host. A body holding the ferrule, and below it the latch column - a 3.3 stem off the body, a 4.3 shoulder standing proud of it, then the 2.3 tab. Occupies an `lc` bore at its `mate` and presents `lc-plug` at its rear for a boot. No depth (provenance.size).
components.name: lc-plug

components.description: A straight MCX crimp plug on a coax cable, seen from the face: the ribbed snap-on grip, the crimp ferrule and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Its slotted outer contact goes inside the jack and is not drawn. Seats in an `mcx` jack at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the stub's far end.
components.name: mcx-plug

components.description: A moulded straight USB 2.0 Micro-B cable plug on its cable, seen from the cable end as a front elevation sees it seated: the overmould at the largest section the Micro-USB specification allows, keyed by the two chamfered corners on its latch side, the round strain relief and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats in a `micro-usb-b` receptacle at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the far end of the stub.
components.name: micro-usb-b-plug
components.size-notes: both figures are the overmould MAXIMUM the Micro-USB specification dimensions on figure 4-5, not a measured plug; one held cable assembly drawing is 11 by 6.9

components.description: A 12-fibre MPO/MTP plug, front view - the 12.5 x 7.6 barrel-ended housing with the MT ferrule standing in its window and the key rib across the top face. UNPINNED: the pins live on the module receptacle this lands in, so this is the female half - stated in `provenance.gender` and not as a field, because the schema carries no key for it yet. Occupies an `mpo` aperture (std/mpo@2 and anything composing it) at its own `mate` point, and presents `mpo-plug` at its rear so a boot or a bare cable can seat there - the shape generic/lc-plug@2 already has, with nothing built yet to take it up. generic/mpo24-plug@1 is the same housing with a two-row ferrule; the fibre count is a property of the ferrule and not of the outline, which is why they are two parts and not one with an attr.
components.name: mpo12-plug

components.description: A 16-fibre MPO/MTP-16 plug, front view - the 12.5 x 7.6 housing of the MPO-12 plug with a key rib that is narrower and OFFSET from the centreline, and a one-row sixteen-fibre MT ferrule between guide-pin bores 5.3 apart. UNPINNED: the pins live on the module receptacle this lands in - stated in `provenance.gender`, because the schema carries no key for it yet. Occupies an `mpo16` aperture (std/mpo16@1 and anything composing it) at its own `mate` point, and presents `mpo16-plug` at its rear so a boot or a bare cable can seat there, with nothing built yet to take it up. It does not mate `mpo`: the offset key is what keeps a sixteen-fibre plug out of MPO-8/12/24 hardware (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 10).
components.name: mpo16-plug

components.description: A 24-fibre MPO/MTP plug, front view - the SAME 12.5 x 7.6 barrel-ended housing generic/mpo12-plug@1 draws, with a two-row MT ferrule in it. The fibre count is a property of the ferrule and not of the outline, which is why this is its own part rather than an attr on that one (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 10), and why the two contracts agree figure for figure: nothing outside the ferrule window changes with the row count. UNPINNED, the same way. Occupies an `mpo` aperture (std/mpo@2 and anything composing it) at its own `mate` point, and presents `mpo-plug` at its rear so a boot or a bare cable can seat there.
components.name: mpo24-plug

components.description: A straight MRJ21 cable plug on its cable: the 48-position plug of a high-density Ethernet breakout or trunk cable in its die-cast backshell, seen from the cable end as a front elevation sees it seated: the backshell, the heads of its two jackscrews at opposite corners, the moulded boot and a short straight stub of cable whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats on an `mrj21` receptacle at its own mate point; the cable leaves from the far end of the stub. What the cable breaks out to is not part of it.
components.name: mrj21-plug
components.size-notes: both figures are SCALED from a drawing that dimensions nothing of the plug; 29.0 is the backshell across and 16.4 the diameter of the boot, which is wider than the 15.7 the backshell is thick

components.description: A NEMA 5-20P straight-blade plug (20 A 125 V, two pole, three wire, grounding), face on: the grip, the face, the round earth pin, the line blade and the neutral blade turned a quarter - the 5-20 key. The input plug at the end of a 120 V 20 A PDU's cord.
components.name: nema-5-20p-plug

components.description: A NEMA L5-20P locking plug (20 A 125 V, two pole, three wire, grounding), face on: the grip, the face and its three curved blades, the earth blade with its bent tab. The input plug at the end of a 120 V PDU's cord.
components.name: nema-l5-20p-plug

components.description: A NEMA L6-20P locking plug (20 A 250 V, two pole, three wire, grounding), face on: the grip, the face and its three curved blades, the earth blade with its bent tab. The input plug at the end of a PDU's cord, which is what identifies the PDU's power input.
components.name: nema-l6-20p-plug

components.description: A generic OSFP with an LC duplex face - the shape of the OSFP optic with two LC bores, standing for all of them. The finned heat sink across the top of the module, a nose below it that stands out of the cage with two keyed bores in it, latch up, and a pull tab. Which module it is - rate, reach, wavelength, watts - is a fact about a vendor product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 5), never here. generic/osfp-mpo16@1 is the same module with the other face.

Which module it is - rate, reach, wavelength, watts - is a fact about a vendor product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 5), never here.

components.description: A generic QSFP cable end - the shape every QSFP+, QSFP28 and QSFP56 direct attach, active copper and active optical cable end has, standing for all of them. The body in the cage is the QSFP envelope; outside it stand the diecast head, a strain relief, a short straight stub of cable and a pull strap lying on the cable and ending in a ring. The cable diameter and the jacket and strap colours are fields. The kind of cable, its rate and its length belong on the vendor wrapper (docs/pluggables-cables-design.md).
components.name: qsfp-cable

components.description: A generic QSFP-DD cable end with the Type 1 head - the shape a direct-attach, active copper, active electrical or active optical QSFP-DD cable has when its backshell stays within the Type 1 20 MAX outside the cage. Inside the cage it is the QSFP-DD module envelope. Outside it: the closed head, a strain-relief boot, a flat pull strap lying on top of the cable and ending in a ring, and a short stub of cable whose diameter and colour are fields. The longer Type 2 head is its own part, generic/qsfp-dd-cable-type2. Which cable it is - its kind, rate and gauge - is a fact about a vendor's product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-cables-design.md decisions 1 and 5), never here.
components.name: qsfp-dd-cable

components.description: A generic QSFP-DD cable end with the longer Type 2 head - the shape a direct-attach, active copper, active electrical or active optical QSFP-DD cable has when its backshell stands more than the Type 1 20 MAX out of the cage. Inside the cage it is the QSFP-DD module envelope. Outside it: the closed head, a strain-relief boot, a flat pull strap lying on top of the cable and ending in a grip, and a short stub of cable whose diameter and colour are fields. Which cable it is - its kind, rate and gauge - is a fact about a vendor's product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-cables-design.md decisions 1 and 5), never here.
components.name: qsfp-dd-cable-type2

components.description: A generic QSFP-DD with an LC duplex face - the shape every QSFP-DD, QSFP-DD800 and QSFP112 optic with two LC bores has, standing for all of them. Two keyed bores with the ferrules standing in them, and a pull tab standing proud of the body because the module is seated. Which module it is - rate, reach, wavelength, watts - is a fact about a vendor's product and lives on the wrapper that composes this (docs/pluggables-design.md, decision 5), never here. Copies generic/qsfp-lc@1 and changes the family: same width and height by design (QSFP-DD HW Rev 6.3 section 1 - the QSFP-DD cage accepts a QSFP module), a longer paddle card behind the same front cross-section.

A duplex-shaped receptacle shell with the one keyed bore in its LEFT bay, where the duplex face has its transmit bore, and the right bay empty; keyway up, under a pull tab. components.description: A one-hole insulated ring terminal crimped on its wire, seen in plan as a front elevation sees it landed on a terminal screw: the ring tongue, the blue sleeve over the crimp barrel, a short straight stub of insulated wire leaving the sleeve in the plane of the face, and the head of the screw that holds it. Seats on a `terminal-stud` terminal at the centre of its stud hole; the wire leaves from the far end of the stub. It is a nominal lug chosen for the library, for 16 to 14 AWG wire, and not the lug of any one device.

components.size-notes: the width is the tongue width B of the JST FV2-MS3; the height is that terminal's overall length L, 17.4, and the 10 stub of wire, a rule and not a reading

components.description: A six-position modular telephone plug (RJ11) on its cord: a small clear rectangular body with a spring latch on its underside that engages the latch slot of a jack, drawn as generic/rj45-plug@1 is drawn, with a short straight stub of cord whose diameter is the cable-od field. Occupies an `rj11` jack at its own mate point; the cord leaves from the far end of the stub. LIKE generic/rj45-plug@1 it has a class-wide depth - see `provenance.size`.
components.name: rj11-plug
components.size-notes: the three figures are dimensioned on one maker's drawing, which marks its dimensions for reference; h is the body without the latch, as on generic/rj45-plug@1

components.description: An RJ45 (8P8C) copper plug, the UNSHIELDED variant - a rectangular body with a spring latch on its underside that engages a jack's latch slot. Occupies a `rj45` receptacle (std/rj45@2 and anything that composes it) at its own `mate` point, and in turn presents `rj45-plug` so a boot (or a bare cable, when there is no boot) can seat on its rear. UNLIKE generic/lc-plug@2, this plug HAS a class-wide depth - see `provenance.size`.
components.name: rj45-plug

components.description: A moulded Anderson Saf-D-Grid cord plug on its cord, seen from the cable end as a front elevation sees it seated: the moulded body, the ribbed strain relief, which is taller than it is wide, and a short straight stub of cord whose diameter is the cable-od field. Seats in a `saf-d-grid` inlet at its own mate point; the cord leaves from the stub's far end.
components.name: saf-d-grid-plug

components.description: An SC fibre plug, front view - the square keyed silhouette an SC connector presents end-on: a 7.4 x 9.0 housing with the 2.5 mm ferrule on its axis and a 0.9 x 1.8 key standing off one long wall, drawn to the LEFT unrotated so it enters std/sc-bore@1, whose keyway is on the left unrotated too. Occupies an `sc` receptacle (std/sc-bore@1 and anything composing it) at its own `mate` point, and in turn presents `sc-plug` so a boot (or a bare cable) can seat on its rear - the shape generic/lc-plug@2 already has, with no `common/sc-boot` built yet to take it up. components.description: Nokia FELT-B (3FE 69486 AA and 3FE 69486 AB), the high-speed point-to-point Ethernet LT of the 7360 ISAM FX / Lightspan FX: eighteen SFP cages in nine ganged 1x2 blocks, grouped G1-G5, each taking a CSFP (two FE/GE ports), an SFP (FE/GE/2.5G) or an SFP+ (10G), so 36, 18 or 16 ports; a BITS OUT RJ45; the PWR(A/S) and ALM lamps and two link lamps per cage. Authored upright, as the card stands in the FX-16; the FX-4 and FX-8 bays turn it 90 degrees. The AA and AB variants share one face (the two UDS chapters embed the SAME image objects for their front and 3D views), so they are one component with the variant in attrs. FELT-B AC (3FE 69486 AC) has no data sheet in any staged document and is not modelled.

components.description: Nokia FGLT-A (3FE 66721 AB), the 16-port GPON line termination board with traffic manager (version A) of the 7360 ISAM FX; dropped from the Lightspan FX guides. Seats in any LT slot of the FX-4, FX-8 and FX-16. Authored upright, as the Unit Data Sheet guides draw it: a thumbscrew and a grey ejector lever in a cap at each end, the PWR and ALM lamps and a hot-surface mark under the top cap, then eight windows in a flat faceplate, each showing two SFP cages angled on a sawtooth behind the plate (16 GPON ports), and the barcode and model labels above the bottom cap. One PON lamp per port sits in the side of its socket, on the port's left. The face is the FGLT-B's; only the model label differs.

components.description: Nokia LPWR-F, the DC power module of the Lightspan MF-8 shelf, in its two builds: LPWR-F AA (3FE 79723 AA, maximum 80 A, a 2 x 40 A breaker) and LPWR-F AB (3FE 79723 AB, maximum 100 A, a 2 x 50 A breaker). Two sit side by side in the PWR 1 and PWR 2 slots at the foot of the slot area and give the shelf power redundancy. Left to right: a module locking screw, the elevated connector block under its semi-transparent door (the two-stud BAT terminal showing through the left half, the energy hazard label covering the right half over the two-stud RET terminal, the door lock and the PWR lamp at its lower left), the circuit breaker with its ON/OFF rocker and the current marker beneath it, the handle, the second locking screw and the ESD mark. The two builds have one face and differ only in the printed marker, which is the `rating` field: "2 X 40A" on the AA, "2X 50A" on the AB.

components.description: Nokia LWLT-C (3FE 76353 AA, and 3FE 76353 BA, the US-made BEAD build), the 16-port Multi-PON line termination board of the Lightspan MF shelves: GPON, XGS-PON or Multi-PON (MPM, GPON + XGS-PON) on every port and 25GS-PON on the even ports, in sixteen SFP-DD cages marked 01 to 16. Authored lying flat, as the MF-8 seats it when the shelf is mounted horizontally: a slate plate with an ejector lever at each lower corner, the board name, the PWR and ALM lamps and a label at the left, and one row of sixteen cages on a 19.9 mm pitch, each on its own sawtooth step turned to face right, with four vent openings above it and, on the strip under the row, its numeral between two rectangular PON light pipes. components.description: The horizontal front dust filter assembly of the Nokia Lightspan MF-8: the perforated front cover that hangs on the cover hook of the shelf's left flange and locks, by two quarter-turn D-ring screws, onto the cable tray fixed to the shelf's right side. It carries the full-size front dust filter (3FE 77351 CA) clamped behind it. It is not orderable on its own: it comes in the horizontal mounting and front cover kits (3TJ 00014 AA for a 19 in. rack, 3TJ 00007 AA for 21 in., 3TJ 00116 AA for 23 in.). It is 507.6 mm wide, wider than the shelf's 481 mm rack face, and overhangs the right flange to cover the cable tray. A different part from the vertical front dust filter assembly 3TJ 00003 AA (355 x 542), which fits only a vertically mounted shelf.

components.description: Nokia 7750 SR-7 / SR-12 (7450 ESS-7 / ESS-12) card-slot impedance panel, the factory-fitted blank for an empty full-length card slot - an IOM or IMM slot, and an empty SF/CPM slot A or B. A plain plate the length of a card, its two short end tabs inset top and bottom, each carrying a flat-blade captive screw. The guides give it no part number. Authored horizontal, like the cards it replaces: the SR-7 seats it at rotate 0 and the SR-12 at rotate 90.
components.name: sr-7-12-slot-impedance-panel
components.size-notes: the SR-7/SR-12 card-slot face (425.4 x 35.4), borrowed from the cards the panel replaces: no guide dimensions the panel. The SR-7 front figure draws it 425.1 long over the same slot the IOMs fill.

components.description: The air filter assembly of the 7750 SR-7 / 7450 ESS-7: a reusable filter tray faceplate with the replaceable filter tray (3HE00190AA, "FLT - 7x50 SR/ESS-7 AIR FILTER") held to it by a Velcro strip. It slides in upright at the left of the chassis rear, beside the fan tray, and filters the air entering at the chassis's right side. The face is the faceplate: plain sheet metal with a captive screw at the top and at the bottom of its right edge and a pull handle. Inspect monthly and replace the filter tray when dirty.
components.name: sr-7-air-filter
components.size-notes: no document states the faceplate's size; measured on the chassis rear, SR7 Fig 8 p51

components.description: Nokia Enhanced Fan Tray of the 7750 SR-7 / 7450 ESS-7, the chassis's single hot-swappable cooling unit. It fills the large bay at the rear, right of the air filter faceplate, and exhausts the air drawn in through the right-side intake. Its rear face is plain sheet metal with two round honeycomb fan grilles at the right, a mounting hole either side of each, and three screw flanges along the top and three along the bottom holding four captive screws a side. The handles are on the tray's sides, not its face. It has no lamp: fan status shows on the CPM (Fan 1-3). It supersedes the High Flow Fan tray.
components.name: sr-7-fan-tray

components.description: Nokia DC PEM-3 100A, the power entry module of the 7750 SR-7 and 7450 ESS-7. Two are factory-installed in rear power bays 1 and 2 and share the load; one carries the whole chassis, two give 1+1. Each PEM-3 connects inside the chassis to its own DC 100A power supply filter in the front filter bay of the same number (nokia/sr-7-power-filter). Its rear face carries a single-feed -48 VDC / RTN terminal block (two studs per pole, for a two-hole lug) under a clear safety cover with a U notch round the left captive screw, the ON/OFF circuit breaker, a pull handle, the second captive screw, and the printed "Model 7750 SR-7 / 100A PEM-3" with two hazard triangles. It has no lamp: its status shows on the CPM (Pwr 1-2). Authored as drawn in power bay 1 (terminal block at the left).
components.name: sr-7-pem-3

components.description: The filler panel that closes an empty rear power bay of the 7750 SR-7 / 7450 ESS-7 when a DC PEM-3 is removed and not replaced at once. Nokia names it only in the removal procedure and gives it no figure and no part number, so it is drawn as a plain plate the size of the PEM-3 face, held by two captive screws where the PEM-3's are.
components.name: sr-7-pem-blank
components.size-notes: borrowed from nokia/sr-7-pem-3@1, the module whose bay the blank closes; no document dimensions the blank

occupant-attrs.data-description: the DE-9 power-supply monitoring port, which takes the Eltek AC shelf's status cable (SR7 p146)

components.description: Nokia DC 100A Power Supply Filter (3HE04498AA; the 7450 ESS-7 orders it as 3HE04500AA), the EMI filter that sits in a front filter bay of the 7750 SR-7 and is wired inside the chassis to the DC PEM-3 in the rear power bay of the same number (nokia/sr-7-pem-3). Two are factory-installed, one per PEM-3. The plate carries a long handle slot, a DE-9 power-supply monitoring port (for the Eltek AC shelf's Y status cable), two hazard triangles, two label plates, four panel screws and a large captive screw at each lower corner. The ESS-7 can close both bays behind nokia/sr-7-psf-safety-panel.

monitoring.description: the DE-9 power-supply monitoring port, which takes the Eltek AC shelf's status cable (SR7 p146)

components.name: sr-7-power-filter
components.size-notes: no document states the filter's size; measured on the chassis front, SR7 Fig 6 p49

attrs.model: SR-7 Power Supply Filter bay safety panel

components.description: The Power Supply Filter bay safety panel of the 7450 ESS-7 / 7750 SR-7: one honeycomb-vented cover that screws over the lower front of the chassis and closes both DC power supply filter bays at once, as the ESS-7 front view draws it. It spans the full chassis width, from the bottom of SF/CPM slot B to the foot of the face, and is held by two slotted screws at its upper corners. It is removed to reach the filters. No part number is given.
components.name: sr-7-psf-safety-panel
components.size-notes: measured on SR7 Fig 7 p50; no document states it. It is LARGER than the two filter bays (437.4 x 64.5 across the two): see provenance.size

components.description: Nokia ACC - 7750 SR-e CCM Impedance Panel (3HE10295AA), the blank for an unused CCM slot (CCM A or CCM B) at the front of the SR-1e, SR-2e and SR-3e: a plain plate with notched lower corners and a captive screw at each upper corner, where the CCM-e's screws are. Authored horizontal.
components.name: sr-e-ccm-impedance-panel
components.size-notes: the CCM-e face (193.0 x 35.4), borrowed: the panel fills the same slot and no guide dimensions it.

components.description: Nokia ACC - 7750 SR-e CPM Impedance Panel (3HE10296AA), the blank for an unused CPM slot at the rear of the SR-1e, SR-2e and SR-3e: a plain plate with a captive screw on a raised tab at each top corner, as the cpm-e carries, and ends shorter than its middle where the card's ejector levers would sit. Authored horizontal.
components.name: sr-e-cpm-impedance-panel
components.size-notes: nokia/cpm-e@1's face (259.1 x 35.4), borrowed: the panel fills the same slot and no guide dimensions it.

components.description: Nokia ACC - 7750 SR-e IOM Impedance Panel (3HE10297AA), the blank for an unused IOM slot at the rear of the SR-1e, SR-2e and SR-3e: a plain plate with a captive screw on a raised tab at each top corner, as the iom-e carries, and ends shorter than its middle where the card's ejector levers would sit. Authored horizontal.
components.name: sr-e-iom-impedance-panel
components.size-notes: nokia/iom-e@1's face (259.1 x 70.8), borrowed: the panel fills the same slot and no guide dimensions it.

components.description: Nokia ACC - SR-e MDA Impedance Panel (3HE10312AA), the blank for an unused MDA slot: a plain plate in the MDA envelope, full height between the two notched lower corners, with a captive screw on each lower end wing. The same part number fills an empty MDA-e slot of the SR-1e, SR-2e and SR-3e and an empty MDA-e-XP slot of the SR-1, which ships with one in slot 2. Authored horizontal.
components.name: sr-e-mda-impedance-panel
components.size-notes: the MDA envelope of the wave-1 convention (193.0 x 35.4), borrowed: no guide dimensions the panel itself. The panel IS an MDA-slot occupant in both the SR-1 and the SR-e, which is the proof that the two slot families are one size.

components.description: Nokia PSU - 7750 SR-e AC (3HE09549AA), the hot-swap universal-AC supply of the SR-1e, SR-2e and SR-3e rear PSU shelf: the integrated exhaust fan at the left behind a red horizontal handle, the Pwr/Stat lamp above the handle's end, an IEC 60320 C14 inlet turned on its side inside a wire cord retainer, and the spring latch at the lower right. Authored horizontal as the guide draws it; the SR-2e and SR-3e seat it upright in PSU 1-6 with `rotate: 90`.

status-leds.description: the one PSU status lamp

components.name: sr-e-psu-ac
components.size-notes: SRE p85 Table 28 prints "H x W x D 3.4 x 7.78 x 1.59 in" - transposed: the face is 3.4 in (86.4) wide and 1.59 in (40.4) tall, and 7.78 in (197.6) is the depth.

components.description: Nokia PSU - 7750 SR-e DC -48V (3HE09548AA), the hot-swap -48/-60 VDC supply of the SR-1e, SR-2e and SR-3e rear PSU shelf: the integrated exhaust fan at the left under a red handle running corner to corner, an M4 ground screw, the Pwr/Stat lamp at the top right, a two-stud barrier terminal block (Batt and RTN) and the spring latch at the lower right. Authored horizontal as the guide draws it; the SR-2e and SR-3e seat it upright in PSU 1-6 with `rotate: 90`.

status-leds.description: the one Pwr/Stat lamp

components.name: sr-e-psu-dc
components.size-notes: SRE p85 Table 28 prints "H x W x D 3.4 x 7.78 x 1.57 in" - transposed: the face is 3.4 in wide and 1.57 in (39.9) tall. h is held at the AC supply's 40.4 so one PSU bay fits both.

components.description: Nokia ACC - 7750 SR-e PSU Impedance Panel (3HE09419AA), the blank for an unused PSU slot of the SR-1e, SR-2e and SR-3e rear shelf: a plain plate the size of a PSU face with a diagonal pull handle and a ribbed latch tab at the lower right. Authored horizontal like the supplies; the SR-2e and SR-3e seat it upright in PSU 1-6 with `rotate: 90`.
components.name: sr-e-psu-impedance-panel
components.size-notes: the SR-e PSU face (86.4 x 40.4), borrowed: the panel fills a PSU slot and no guide dimensions it.
